question: How an AI ROC and validation-selected operating points compare with historical clinical reader decisions under different cohort definitions, and how numerical CIs qualify the selected performance differences.

observations.whole: Two adjacent ROC panels share full 0–1 axes. UK panel has inset, three distinct clinical marker shapes, orange AI crosses and delta annotation. US panel has two purple line styles, one clinical benchmark and two AI operating points. No interval bars or confidence band appear in the original graphic.
observations.detail: UK gray region is an inset locator, not a confidence region. The inset enlarges near x=.04–.12 and y=.62–.70, identifies i/ii/iii thresholds, and links first-reader point to threshold i with a dashed guide. Crosses are operating points, not error bars.
observations.transfer_omission: The new graphic deliberately discards the ROC/inset geometry and uses published Table 2a CIs; no curve coordinates were digitized.

interval.definition: confidence interval on difference, method varies by cohort
interval.UK: Wald using Obuchowski variance for paired binomial proportions, adjusted for reader clustering
interval.US: bootstrap, 1000 replications, inverse probability weighted observations; resampling algorithm and interval recipe not specified in inspected Methods

uncertainty.paired_comparison: Same eligible case has an AI prediction and a historical clinical reader decision. Test case is one selected mammogram examination per woman. Different reader identities constitute clusters in UK analysis. The US bootstrap resampling unit is not explicitly described, despite case-level pairing.
uncertainty.n_definition: Endpoint-specific cases with available clinical read: cancer cases for sensitivity, non-cancer cases for specificity; unweighted N while US estimates are weighted.
uncertainty.source_priority: transcribe publisher Table 2 delta/CI/N columns verbatim in precision; main Results is rounding cross-check
uncertainty.unit_conversion: percentage difference is represented as percentage points, numeric values unchanged
uncertainty.selection: Four main clinical comparisons in Results; two metrics for UK first reader and US clinical reader, system trained on UK+US. No unselected comparison is inferred.
uncertainty.excluded: No raw data, error reconstruction, ROC reconstruction, pooling, P values, independent-country ranking, retraining, SD-to-CI conversion or seed inference.

support_bounds: CIs quantify paired endpoint differences in retrospective evaluation; they are neither patient risk nor random-seed variation.
Cancer follow-up differs: 39 months UK and 27 months US. A common visual scale does not authorize pooling or comparing the country effects.
The drawn four comparisons use the UK+US-trained system. The original dotted US curve is a separate UK-only-trained generalization experiment, excluded from the redraw.
One exam per woman does not imply every statistical operation was patient-bootstrap; exact US bootstrap mechanism is not described in inspected Methods.
UK sensitivity CI includes zero; preserve absence of a superiority claim. Noninferiority margin is distinct and not drawn.
source_conflicts: Unselected UK consensus specificity row displays equal clinical/AI percentages but delta -3.35; retain source inconsistency without attempting correction.
UK sensitivity published delta 2.70 is not exactly the subtraction of displayed rounded percentages 65.42 and 62.69. We transcribe delta, not calculate a replacement.
Main prose rounds UK specificity to 1.2 [0.29,2.1] and US CIs more coarsely; numerical source priority is official Table 2a.

Public publisher article body is a subscription preview; full Methods read from legal Cambridge accepted manuscript. This mixed-version evidence is declared; Addendum reviewed for updated training details.
Figure 2 panel titles abbreviate follow-up as 3 years (UK) and 2 years (US); caption and cohort Methods define 39 and 27 months. Redraw uses the precise definitions.

layout_rules.rule: Give every interval an estimand, uncertainty type, confidence level, statistical unit and method; group rows when methods differ.
layout_rules.condition: A result panel mixes cohorts, endpoints or analysis methods.

layout_rules.rule: Preserve direct reported difference CIs; marginal metric CIs and rounded point percentages cannot supply paired-difference CIs.
layout_rules.condition: Comparing model and clinician on the same cases.

layout_rules.rule: Display endpoint-specific N with its class/level and note whether estimates are weighted.
layout_rules.condition: Sensitivity and specificity use different denominator subsets, or enrichment weights are used.

layout_rules.rule: Use a zero reference for differences and show the full interval even when it crosses zero.
layout_rules.condition: CIs include both negative and positive differences; do not hide one side or annotate all rows as superiority.

layout_rules.rule: Separate SD across seeds/readers from sampling CI; do not silently convert or treat 1000 resamples as N.
layout_rules.condition: Any error bar or uncertainty label.

layout_rules.rule: A source ROC needs threshold-level scores; scalar differences and intervals support a new point+CI graph only.
layout_rules.condition: Only aggregate numerical results are legally available.

nontransferable: All study-specific values, CIs, sample counts, follow-up periods, weighting and thresholds.
Retrospective results do not establish clinical deployment benefit, device-general performance or prospective effectiveness.
Public access to a manuscript does not license redistribution of the original figures.
The bootstrap interval construction and resampling scheme cannot be invented from a generic bootstrap convention.

uncertainty_type_rules.meaning: variation of a metric over those runs
uncertainty_type_rules.boundary: Not a patient-sampling CI. Run count cannot replace endpoint N. No run replicates are available in this case.

uncertainty_type_rules.unit: must specify observations, clusters and weighting
uncertainty_type_rules.meaning: An outcome SD, estimator SE and across-replicate SD are different quantities, even when written in percent.
uncertainty_type_rules.boundary: Do not derive an unweighted binomial interval from an aggregate percentage plus N when pairing, reader clustering or sampling weights matter.

uncertainty_type_rules.meaning: between-reader dispersion, distinct from mean-reader or paired-difference CI
uncertainty_type_rules.boundary: The paper has a separate six-reader analysis; its SD cannot be used as any of the four plotted error bars.

uncertainty_type_rules.unit: must be stated by source; multiple records must retain patient clustering when applicable
uncertainty_type_rules.meaning: resampling-based uncertainty in a specified estimator
uncertainty_type_rules.boundary: In this paper, one selected case per woman establishes observation level, while the exact US bootstrap algorithm is not described in inspected Methods. Do not promote that inference to an explicit patient-bootstrap recipe.

uncertainty_type_rules.meaning: A stated confidence level and construction attached to the exact estimand
uncertainty_type_rules.boundary: The UK difference CI uses Wald/Obuchowski, not the DeLong AUC method. US uses reported bootstrap CI, not an invented percentile or BCa interval.
